html:
A mellah is the walled Jewish quarter of a Moroccan town. The first was set up in Fez in 1438, when the Jews of the city were moved next to the royal palace, for protection and control. Other towns followed.

Jews had lived in Morocco since ancient times, and were joined by refugees after the expulsion from Spain in 1492. In the mellahs they had their own synagogues, schools and courts, and worked as merchants, craftsmen and royal agents.

In 1948 Morocco had the largest Jewish community in the Arab world, about a quarter of a million people. Most left in the next decades, for Israel, France and Canada, part of the Jewish exodus from Arab lands. Moroccan Jews remain one of the largest groups in Israel.
